data.cultural_impact: The name Firwad is associated with the story of Prophet Sulaiman and his companions in Islamic history. Firwad is remembered for possessing the unique ability to split the moon, which demonstrates power and individual strength. This story can inspire a cultural appreciation for Islamic history and the heroic qualities of its companions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Firwad also holds spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of the power and strength granted by Allah to His servants. This name can inspire individuals to strive for personal growth and develop inner strength to overcome challenges in their lives. It also highlights the idea of being used as a vessel for Allah's will and demonstrates that anything is possible with faith and determination.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 10, Page 186-187 The name Firwad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: Year 26 AH (647 AD) during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab
historical_references.context: Firwad ibn Abi Manqal was a Christian king of Al-Jabal (modern Lebanon). He made a treaty with Umar ibn Al-Khattab that allowed Muslims to practice their religion peacefully in his lands. However, Firwad later broke the treaty and attacked the Muslims. Umar led a military campaign against Firwad and defeated him, after which Firwad converted to Islam and submitted to Umar.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf, Volume 5, Page 142-143 The name Firwad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: Year 35 AH (655 AD) during the caliphate of Ali ibn Abi Talib
historical_references.context: Firwad ibn Abi Manqal, the king of Al-Jabal, refused to pay the annual tribute to the Muslims. Ali sent an army under the command of Qaid ibn Amr Al-Hilali to collect the tribute. Firwad was defeated and he sought refuge in a fortress. The Muslims besieged the fortress and after a long struggle, Firwad was killed. His son, Harith ibn Firwad, succeeded him and continued to resist the Muslims. However, he was eventually defeated and converted to Islam.
